title: Come, Said Jesus' Sacred Voice
description: Come, Said Jesus' Sacred Voice in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Anna Laetitia Barbauld wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 121, “Christ's Invitations”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, said Je-sus' sa-cred voice, Come and make my paths your choice; I will guide you to your home; Wea-ry pil-grim! hith-er come.

lines: Come, said Jesus' sacred voice,
Come and make my paths your choice;
I will guide you to your home;
Weary pilgrim! hither come.
Thou who, houseless, sole, forlorn,
Long hast borne the proud world's scorn,
Long hast roamed the barren waste,
Weary pilgrim! hither haste.
Ye who, tossed on beds of pain,
Seek for ease, and seek in vain;
Ye whose swoln and sleepless eyes
Watch to see the morning rise;
Ye, by fiercer anguish torn,
In remorse for guilt who mourn,
Here repose your heavy care;
Who the stings of sin can bear?
Sufferer! come, for here is found
Balm that flows for every wound;
Peace that ever shall endure,
Rest eternal, sacred, sure.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Anna Laetitia Barbauld died in 1825.
credits: Words by Anna Laetitia Barbauld (1743–1825), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
